blocks.text: Project: Roadway Widening Study for {{fact:f:E-2005-001.client}}. Subject: working session on the existing conditions and the widening options for the corridor. Prepared by Linda George, Project Engineer.

The session confirmed that the study has moved past the compilation of the record and onto the corridor itself, and it settled three matters: that the existing-conditions base is sound enough to build the options on, that two utility conflicts along the corridor will govern which of the widening options remain workable, and that the owner will supply the traffic counts and the current site plan on which the geometry and the corridor limits depend.

Linda George opened by walking the meeting through the existing-conditions base as it now stands, describing the survey coverage of the roadway and its right-of-way, the record information gathered on the utilities in the corridor, and the field observations taken to confirm what the records show, and it was agreed that the base has reached the stage at which the widening options can be laid out on it without the risk that a later correction to the base would undo the work already done.

Jeffrey Perez reported on the utility and drainage information he has posted to the base sheets, noting in particular two points at which an existing utility sits within the width the widened roadway would have to take, and it was discussed that these two conflicts are the constraints most likely to decide among the widening options, so that each option carried forward will be tested against them before it is developed in any further detail.

James Skinner set out what the owner needs from the study, which is a clear account of what the widening requires and of what it will cost, and he agreed to furnish the traffic counts and the current site plan for the development, both of which the geometry and the corridor limits depend upon, and it was understood on all sides that the options cannot be fixed until those two items are in hand.

On the schedule it was noted that the study stands in its early phase, with the existing conditions established and the options not yet compared, and that the pace from this point will be set by how quickly the traffic counts and the site plan are returned, since the geometry cannot be fixed nor the cost opinion begun until the corridor limits are settled against the owner's current plan for the site.

rows: Lay out the widening options on the confirmed existing-conditions base
Test each option against the two utility conflicts in the corridor
Furnish the traffic counts and the current site plan
Confirm the corridor limits once the site plan is in hand
On receipt of the site plan

blocks.text: The next working session will be scheduled once the widening options are laid out and the traffic counts are in hand, so that the session can be spent on comparing the options rather than on establishing the base a second time.
